title: The First Laugh
subtitle: Joy can coexist with grief
sourceCredit: Charlotte Cline · The Moth Radio Hour, “Saving Graces”

shot.title: The quiet table
shot.direction: A grieving family shares a dinner table with nearly empty bubbles and a photograph on the mantel.
shot.soundDirection: Long room hush, an absurd muffled interruption, gentle spontaneous laughter.

illustration.direction: Wide dining room with two family members seated naturally at a table, grounded legs and chairs visible. Their shoulders are tired, hands still near plain cups. A small lit photograph on the mantel stays in the same room. The silence has weight; no giant bubbles or grief icons.

illustration.direction: Both at the table with a small surprised pause. The man turns toward the woman with lifted brows and a half-open mouth; she keeps one hand against her cup while processing the interruption. Reaction precedes laughter; preserve seated anatomy and table contact.

illustration.direction: The man’s shoulders soften into one involuntary laugh and he brings a relaxed hand near his chest. The woman begins to smile half a beat later, leaning toward him slightly. Keep the movement small, believable and affectionate; cups stay planted.

actions.direction: His chest catches once, his hand follows against his shirt, then his head gives a small released dip. Her face inclines a moment later; the mugs and table remain still.
